# What GitLab credentials the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is, carried on through the alphabet to the count its kind is
# written to.
#
# GitLab's documentation gives the prefix of each kind and nothing else — no
# length, no alphabet, no checksum. The counts below are the ones GitLab's own
# secret detection ruleset states, and the routable shape is the one its Cells
# design document writes; the pattern's own file says what each of those rests
# on.

patterns: gitlab-token

# The kinds of token GitLab gives both a prefix and a shape, each stated once
# rather than assumed to follow from the one above it.

case: a personal access token in an environment assignment
in:   GITLAB_TOKEN=glpat-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  GITLAB_TOKEN=«gitlab-token»

case: a deploy token
in:   gldt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a runner authentication token
in:   glrt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a runner authentication token created through a registration token
in:   glrtr-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a feed token
in:   glft-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a scim oauth token
in:   glsoat-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a feature flags client token
in:   glffct-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: an incoming mail token
in:   glimt-0123456789abcdefghijklmno
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a pipeline trigger token
in:   glptt-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCD
out:  «gitlab-token»

# The pipeline trigger token is the one kind GitLab's own ruleset writes two
# counts for, twenty characters behind the prefix or forty, and both are read.
# The case above this comment is a run of exactly forty. The four below it are a
# run reaching only the shorter count, a run reaching past the shorter but not
# the longer, a run reaching past the longer, and a run one character short of
# the shorter — where nothing is located at all.

case: a pipeline trigger token written to the shorter of its two counts
in:   glptt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a pipeline trigger token whose run falls between its two counts
in:   glptt-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrst
out:  «gitlab-token»klmnopqrst

case: a pipeline trigger token whose run is longer than its longer count
in:   glptt-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHI
out:  «gitlab-token»EFGHI

case: a pipeline trigger token one short of its shorter count
in:   glptt-0123456789abcdefghi
out:  glptt-0123456789abcdefghi

case: an agent token
in:   glagent-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMN
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: an oauth application secret
in:   gloas-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ01
out:  «gitlab-token»

# A CI/CD job token is the one kind whose classic body carries anything in front
# of it: the partition id of the job, and the underscore closing it.

case: a ci job token
in:   glcbt-0f_0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a ci job token with the longest partition id
in:   glcbt-0123f_0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

# The shape GitLab.com is moving to for Cells. The payload carries the routing
# information and is closed by a dot, the length of the payload and a checksum —
# with a version between the two in the form GitLab writes today. Neither the
# length nor the checksum is read as a number, so both are written from the
# ordered run like everything else here.

case: a routable personal access token
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq.012345678
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a routable personal access token carrying a version
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq.01.012345678
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a routable runner authentication token, whose scope stands in its payload
in:   glrt-t1_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq.012345678
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a routable ci job token, whose partition id stands in its payload
in:   glcbt-0f_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq.012345678
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a payload longer than the shortest one
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEF.012345678
out:  «gitlab-token»

# A token as the text around it is ordinarily written.

case: a token in a clone url
in:   https://oauth2:glpat-0123456789abcdefghij@gitlab.com/group/project.git
out:  https://oauth2:«gitlab-token»@gitlab.com/group/project.git

case: a token in a private token header
in:   PRIVATE-TOKEN: glpat-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  PRIVATE-TOKEN: «gitlab-token»

case: a token in json
in:   {"token":"glpat-0123456789abcdefghij","scopes":["api"]}
out:  {"token":"«gitlab-token»","scopes":["api"]}

case: a runner registration command
in:   gitlab-runner register --url https://gitlab.com --token glrt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  gitlab-runner register --url https://gitlab.com --token «gitlab-token»

case: two tokens of different kinds on one line
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghij gldt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token» «gitlab-token»

# The count a classic body is read to is exact, so a longer run of the alphabet
# is a token and what was written after it. The characters left behind belong to
# no credential if the ones in front of them are a token.

case: an alphabet run longer than a body is a body and what follows it
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghijklmn
out:  «gitlab-token»klmn

case: a hyphen after a token, which is a body character and still not part of one
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghij-backup
out:  «gitlab-token»-backup

# There is no boundary in front of a match either, so a token written against a
# word character is trimmed rather than dropped — and a token can begin inside
# the one before it, which is why the scan resumes one byte along. The two
# values overlap and are redacted as one.

case: a token written against a word character
in:   GITLAB_TOKEN_glpat-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  GITLAB_TOKEN_«gitlab-token»

case: a token beginning inside the token before it
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefglpat-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  «gitlab-token»

# A candidate that falls short of the routable shape is read as a classic token
# rather than left alone, so the dot and what follows it stay in the text.

case: a payload closed by too short a checksum is read as a classic token
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq.01234567
out:  «gitlab-token»klmnopq.01234567

case: a classic token is shorter than a payload, so a dot behind one is text
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghij.012345678
out:  «gitlab-token».012345678

# What the pattern redacts that GitLab did not issue. The alphabet a body is
# read in holds the hyphen and the underscore, so a hyphenated identifier
# written straight after a prefix reaches the count; and a routable payload has
# no count, so a host label of nine lowercase characters written behind one
# reads as a checksum. Both are redacted, because nothing in the text tells
# either from a token — and both are written here so that the day one of them
# stops being redacted is a decision rather than a discovery.

case: a hyphenated identifier of exactly the count behind a prefix
in:   glagent-config-map-0123456789abcdef-production-tokyo-01234
out:  «gitlab-token»

case: a host label of nine characters read as a checksum
in:   glagent-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMN.production.example.com
out:  «gitlab-token»n.example.com

case: a host label of eight characters, which is one short of a checksum
in:   glagent-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMN.internal.example.com
out:  «gitlab-token».internal.example.com

# And what the pattern leaves alone.

case: a body one character too short
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdefghi
out:  glpat-0123456789abcdefghi

case: an incoming mail token at the count of the shorter kinds
in:   glimt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  glimt-0123456789abcdefghij

case: an uppercase prefix
in:   GLPAT-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  GLPAT-0123456789abcdefghij

case: a prefix with no hyphen behind it
in:   glpat0123456789abcdefghij
out:  glpat0123456789abcdefghij

case: a space inside a body
in:   glpat-0123456789abcdef ghij
out:  glpat-0123456789abcdef ghij

case: a workspace token, a kind GitLab publishes no shape for
in:   glwt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  glwt-0123456789abcdefghij

case: a runner registration token, which GitLab removed in 18.0
in:   GR13489410123456789abcdefghij
out:  GR13489410123456789abcdefghij

case: a session cookie, which is named by the text in front of it
in:   _gitlab_session=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  _gitlab_session=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a ci job token with no partition id
in:   glcbt-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  glcbt-0123456789abcdefghij

case: a ci job token with a partition id too long
in:   glcbt-01234f_0123456789abcdefghij
out:  glcbt-01234f_0123456789abcdefghij

case: a prefix that is none of the kinds
in:   glzzz-0123456789abcdefghij
out:  glzzz-0123456789abcdefghij

case: prose holding the two bytes a candidate opens with
in:   the global glossary is a glimpse of a glacier
out:  the global glossary is a glimpse of a glacier
